title: Define Success
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: The eighth Will to Learn strategy addresses a problem Stuart considers pervasive but under-examined: most students have no clear or helpful idea of what success in a given class actually means. He breaks the strategy into its component words, Define, Success, Wisely, Early, Often, and argues success must be both teacher-generated and student-generated. He details the Wlodkowski 2x10 intervention as his go-to for reaching students who seem uninterested in defining success at all, and closes with advice on proactive, low-effort positive parent contact for students whose families are perceived as uninvolved.
points: Stuart frames the strategy's four qualifiers precisely: definitions must be wise, informed by real experience rather than naive slogans, and repeated often since one-and-done won't do it.

The Wlodkowski 2x10 intervention, two minutes of nonacademic conversation for ten straight class days, is his primary tool for reaching students uninterested in succeeding, requiring only 20 total minutes of class time.
His index-card tracking system for 2x10 conversations doubles as a bias check, letting him periodically review whether his selection of students of concern reflects his classroom's actual diversity.

Low-effort positive parent contact, a quick phone call or email highlighting something specific and positive about the student, is framed as a Credibility multiplier extending signaling into the home.
